Lessons.Title: Relate Multiplication and Division
ExplanationParagraphs: Equal-group division corresponds to a missing multiplication factor. If groups×size=total, divide the total by the known factor to find the other.
Source How Many Do You See: six base-ten rods arranged in three rows and two columns. Six rods of ten make 60; use6×10,3×(2×10),or(3×10)×2.

Source Division Round Table (20min): pupils work in groups of four. Box1 create an equal-groups drawing; pass right. Box2 next pupil writes a corresponding division story; pass right. Box3 next pupil writes multiplication with an unknown symbol; pass right. Box4 final pupil writes matching division with an unknown quotient. Return sheet and compare work. These are pupil-created situations, not fixed source numeric exercises.

Source Sets of School Supplies (15min): Kiran32 paper clips at4 per student gives8 students (32÷4);28 books equally in4 stacks gives7 books per stack (28÷4);6 boxes each with8 erasers gives48 erasers (6×8);Lin places36 sticky notes in sets of6 per notebook, giving6 notebooks (36÷6). Students may write logically equivalent equations; a teacher checks units and source context.
Original synthesis relates24÷4=? with4×?=24 (6) and4×?=28 with28÷4=? (7). Distinguish unknown group count from unknown group size.

Independently drawn tens and cards, not publisher source artwork. Original worksheet pixels, student PDF, third-party photograph, protected Sharing Roses Cool-down, runtime tests, Stage D and academic review remain outside this authoring closure.

KeyConcepts.Title: Inverse operations

KeyConcepts.Title: Unknown symbol
KeyConcepts.Definition: The equation uses a sign for the number being found.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Choose which quantity is the unknown from the story.
